decisions.reason: As a large established machinery firm, we would usually give a newly launched complementary system more time because there is no clear evidence yet that its first-year results fall below aspiration levels.

The coolant cleaning centrifuge fits the firm's process-equipment portfolio, and with no observed performance shortfall a slack-rich incumbent would normally continue offering it while learning about demand.
Coolant nozzles are a low-complexity add-on product, so boundedly rational management would be inclined to retain them unless clear underperformance emerges.
A scraper belt chip conveyor is close to the firm's core machinery business, so we would keep it on the market while sales information accumulates over a longer industrial buying cycle.
The magnetic belt chip conveyor appears to be a related line extension, and absent evidence of results below aspiration levels a large German manufacturer would likely continue supporting it.
The hinged belt chip conveyor is another core-adjacent product for which an experienced firm with organisational slack would normally avoid an early withdrawal after only one year.
